fixes.explanation: Ooh, I see why you'd poke at that one, friend, but it's true. Paul says, "He who loves his wife loves himself." He's just said husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies, and then he adds, "…no one ever hated his own body…" (Ephesians 5:29). Think about it: I have never once met a stamper who forgot to look after his own handle. So a husband should care for his wife the same way.

Rome is a fair guess, friend, but it's not in the verse. Paul says, "…He who is both their Master and yours is in heaven…" Picture a boss who thinks he's the top of the whole chart, and then Paul walks in and says there's a Master over him, too. Nobody gets to sit in the corner office on this one, because that Master isn't in any city on the map. He's in heaven.

problems.problem: The explanation still largely repeats the verse, and its illustration lacks a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The boss comparison repeats the point that the masters have a Master without developing its significance.
